title: Why do we need security?
covers: CIA triad, security trends, security policies, legal & ethical aspects
learningGoals: You will be able to distinguish Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability.
You will be able to evaluate real-world trade-offs in security policies.
You will be able to identify ethical and legal duties under cybersecurity laws.

lessonCards.title: The Golden Rule: The CIA Triad
lessonCards.analogy: Imagine a bank vault: locks protect secrets, seals detect stolen gold, and doors permit access.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Security rests on three pillars: Confidentiality hides secrets, Integrity guards data accuracy, and Availability guarantees access.
lessonCards.example: Medical records require privacy (C), tamper-proof logs (I), and 24/7 doctor access (A).

lessonCards.title: Security Policies & Enforcement
lessonCards.analogy: A fire drill rules manual tells employees where to walk before smoke appears.
lessonCards.coreConcept: A security policy is a formal plan of rules governing data access, passcodes, and breach response.
lessonCards.example: Mandating password rotation every 90 days or enforcing zero-trust badge swipes at every door.

lessonCards.title: Ethics & Law in Cyberspace
lessonCards.analogy: A locksmith possesses lockpicks to fix broken doors, never to burgle houses.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Ethical hackers operate under strict authorization. Accessing systems without written permission violates global cybercrime acts.
lessonCards.example: Penetration testers sign a formal Rules of Engagement document before probing corporate firewalls.

questions.prompt: Which pillar of the CIA triad is broken when an attacker alters medical dosage records in a hospital database?
questions.explanation: Integrity guarantees that information remains accurate and unaltered by unauthorized parties.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Modifying stored values breaks integrity.
questions.realWorldExample: In 2016, attackers altered Bangladesh Bank transfer records.

questions.prompt: A ransomware group launches a massive DDoS attack against an emergency dispatch center. Which security pillar is directly targeted?
questions.explanation: Availability ensures services and resources remain accessible to authorized users when needed.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Knocking dispatch systems offline directly destroys availability.
questions.realWorldExample: The 2016 Dyn DNS attack took major services offline across North America.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes an ethical white-hat security researcher from an unauthorized hacker?
questions.explanation: Explicit, legal written authorization from the system owner defines ethical security operations.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Without written permission, accessing computer systems is illegal.
Operating systems are tools, not legal definitions.
questions.realWorldExample: The US Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) prosecutes unauthorized access.

questions.prompt: Which security policy rule best prevents employees from leaking customer database backups on USB sticks?
options: Disabling removable media via endpoint management
questions.explanation: Endpoint controls disable unauthorized USB storage devices.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Disabling mass storage interfaces blocks hardware-based exfiltration.
Wi-Fi passwords do not prevent physical USB copying.
questions.realWorldExample: Stuxnet was transported into air-gapped facilities on infected USB sticks.

questions.prompt: An employee reads their coworker's confidential performance review without permission. Which principle is violated?
questions.explanation: Confidentiality ensures that only authorized individuals can view sensitive information.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Unauthorized reading directly compromises confidentiality.
Fault tolerance allows systems to survive hardware crashes.
questions.realWorldExample: Insider unauthorized snooping causes over 30% of enterprise privacy breaches.

questions.prompt: What is the primary objective of the Principle of Least Privilege?
options: Grant users only minimal permissions required for their tasks
Give all developers root administrator access
Allow all employees to share passwords
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits user and service account rights to strictly what is essential.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Minimal permissions restrict blast radius if an account is compromised.
Root access for all drastically increases security risk.
Open firewall ports create attack surfaces.
questions.realWorldExample: The 2013 Target breach began with compromised HVAC vendor credentials having excessive access.

ashRecap: Confidentiality hides secrets, Integrity guards truth, and Availability keeps the lights on!
